title: Jacobs selected for multi-year Washington DC area airport modernization program
summary: Jacobs has been selected by the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority for a key role in major revitalization projects at Washington Dulles International Airport and Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport through a multi-year program that will modernize and expand two of America’s most iconic aviation gateways.
body_markdown:
DALLAS –


[Jacobs](http://www.jacobs.com/) (NYSE: J) has been selected by the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority (MWAA) for a key role in major revitalization projects at Washington Dulles International Airport and Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport through a multi-year program that will modernize and expand two of America’s most iconic aviation gateways. The program will help the airports accommodate growing passenger demand, improve operational efficiency and create a smoother travel experience while preparing the airports for future growth.


Jacobs will assist MWAA in overseeing a phased modernization that introduces new terminal processing areas, improves passenger circulation and updates aging concourses with more efficient, future-ready technology and infrastructure.


Support services to be provided under a five-year contract, which could be extended for additional years, may include staff augmentation for administrative and technical engineering tasks, engineering oversight of project design, environmental program support, project controls, contract administration and construction management.


**Jacobs Chair and CEO Bob Pragada said:** “Washington Dulles and Reagan National are among the most renowned airports in the world, and this revitalization gives us the opportunity to build on their legacy. Our focus is on creating a travel experience that is simpler, faster and more connected, while also preparing the airports to meet long‑term demand. Together with the U.S. Department of Transportation and MWAA, we’re blending thoughtful modernization with the timeless architecture that makes these spaces unique, ensuring the airports continue to serve as a proud gateway to the U.S. national capital for decades to come."


**Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority, President & CEO Jack Potter said:** "Package T, which is an extension of the airport’s underground train system and related work, is a key component of our Dulles Global Gateway initiative to transform and modernize the Washington area’s premier international airport. Jacobs, with its blend of aviation, rail and transportation experience, including work on the Airports Authority’s recent construction of the Metrorail Silver Line project, will be instrumental in moving this important project forward."


Planned improvements across landside, terminal and airfield operations aim to make the passenger journey easier from end to end. Updated check‑in, security and baggage systems will reduce wait times and improve passenger flow. New concourse connectors will provide direct links between the concourses, giving travelers more predictable routes through the terminal. Inside the concourses, added natural light, expanded gate areas and refreshed amenities will create a more open and comfortable experience.


The modernization also prepares both airports for future growth. At Dulles, new international and domestic concourses and an expanded central processing area will support long-term demand. The program also includes provisions for exploring future mobility enhancements, such as high‑speed moving walkways and small autonomous shuttle technologies to improve how people move through the airports. New retail and dining areas will be located in high‑traffic zones to improve convenience for travelers while supporting airport revenue generation.


**Jacobs Aviation Market Director – Americas Steve Pelham said** : “Modernizing airports while they remain fully operational requires careful planning, smart construction sequencing and close collaboration among airport operators, airlines and project delivery organizations. Working alongside MWAA, United Airlines and other stakeholders, we’ll deliver improvements that enhance the passenger experience, strengthen connectivity and accommodate future growth at Washington Dulles.”
